reasons: F01, F02: material weakness in financial close/reporting means the controls that produce the statements were not reliable, and F03 means no auditor ICFR opinion was required to test them.
F05, F06: an auditor change within 2 years combined with a disclosed disagreement with accountants is a serious red flag for contested accounting judgments.

F11, F12: material related-party transactions and a 36% revenue concentration in one customer create room for transactions that lack economic substance or are recorded at the wrong amount (gross vs net, round-tripping).

R04, R02, R09: sales grew about 74x and the gross margin index (57.7) collapsed. These extreme swings drive the Beneish M-score (87.8, far above -1.78) and point to a fundamental change in the business model (e.g. low-margin pass-through trading revenue) that needs scrutiny of revenue recognition.
R03, R13: asset quality deteriorated (AQI 1.84) and soft assets are 93% of total assets, so reported asset values depend heavily on judgment (goodwill, intangibles, investments).

F22, F23, F21, R16, R07: a major acquisition, a recent reverse merger/SPAC history, ongoing capital raising, securities issued, and sharply higher leverage (LVGI 9.38) create both pressure and opportunity to present favourable results.
F14, F20: a CEO/CFO change during the year and incentive pay tied to revenue/EPS add management pressure and transition risk.
R19, R08, R10: operating cash flow covers only 0.28 of net income, so earnings quality is weak (though total accruals are negative), and the volatility undermines confidence in reported figures.
Mitigants: F04 no going concern, F07 no prior-period correction, F16-F18 no disclosed investigations or class actions at filing time, R17 F-score 0.62 below threshold.
